title: Memory-matched expert-count and precision comparison: tacodevs REAP25 reference (A) vs REAP160 (B) / HOPE160 (C) / HOPE176 (D)

unit_conventions.byte_rule: Every budget comparison is decided on exact integer bytes. Decimal GB uses 10^9 bytes; GiB uses 2^30 bytes. The two units are never mixed or silently converted.
unit_warnings: EXACT control cap: 100431428728 bytes = 100.431428728 decimal GB = 93.53405677527189 GiB (~93.53 GiB), derived from the archived evidence/tree.json (22 top-level text shards, revision 95d80053eb22112f2acc4244330eb67b4f534c94). All fit comparisons use this exact figure.

The published model-card '100.4 GB' is a ROUNDED LABEL only (= 100400000000 bytes = 93.504786 GiB when read as decimal GB). Never call the rounded card cap the exact baseline; it differs from the exact archived tree sum by 31428728 bytes.
It is NOT 100.4 GiB (which would be 107803679130 bytes = 107.803679 decimal GB).
The original production target 103 GiB = 110595407872 bytes = 110.595408 decimal GB is a DISTINCT cap from A's exact 100431428728-byte archived tree sum.
The existing project weight target 100-105 GiB = 107374182400-112742891520 bytes = 107.374182-112.742892 decimal GB, so A (93.53405677527189 GiB) sits BELOW the project target range.
Do not call A and B/C/D memory matched in prose units; 'memory matched' is decided only by the exact-byte fit rule below.

fit_rule.statement: An arm fits a cap if and only if its measured text_weight_bytes <= cap.weight_bytes. Auxiliary weights, KV cache and runtime headroom are recorded separately and NEVER netted into text weight bytes.
fit_rule.text_weight_bytes_source: exact byte inventory from safetensors headers/index; published GB values are recorded as published, not as measured bytes

per_retained_index.rate_note: official native packing rate; any ROCmFP4/FAST format at >= 4.25 bpw costs at least this much per retained index

feasibility_math_gate.verdict_reason: 160 retained expert indices at 4.25 bpw = 100537466880 B EXPERTS ONLY, over A's entire-text cap 100431428728 B by 106038152 B before any protected non-expert byte; pure ROCmFP4/FAST-160 plus protected non-experts cannot fit the A control cap
feasibility_math_gate.A_control: A remains the mandatory static control; candidates that do not fit are reported as not fitting and unequal weight budgets are never silently called memory matched
feasibility_math_gate.production_103gib: B/C at 160 experts are feasible at the 103 GiB production cap (110595407872 B) with a dynamic precision mix to be planned: native 4.25 experts plus protected non-experts = 109432040320 B, headroom 1163367552 B
feasibility_math_gate.fair_common_cap_comparison_requires: either a cap-matched 192-expert reconstruction from the OFFICIAL Xiaomi source (production lineage), or an explicitly labeled exploration of formats below 4.25 bpw and/or a 144-expert arm; the choice is always stated explicitly
feasibility_math_gate.unchanged: the user's primary 160-expert goal and every original byte budget remain unchanged; this entry records the arithmetic gate only

evaluation_protocol.distribution_controls_are: controls only; token agreement/KL are NOT capability or task-success evidence
evaluation_protocol.decision_metric: held-out long-horizon golden repository task success on the frozen golden set
evaluation_protocol.golden_policy: golden tasks are frozen before calibration and NEVER enter calibration, imatrix, QLoRA, QAT or quant search
evaluation_protocol.published_metrics_note: Published agreement figures (e.g. A: ALL 90.4%, code 90.8%, agent 88.5%, reasoning 94.2%) are distribution metrics, NOT measured task success
evaluation_protocol.conversion_rule: never convert already-quantized MLX checkpoints into production ROCmFP4; official Xiaomi source remains the production lineage and its native MXFP4 quantization (stored MXFP4 independently confirmed) is documented, not concealed; MXFP4 QAT training is a tacodevs card claim only

full_matrix.description: Full comparison matrix for final validation (issue 46), including arms A-D
full_matrix.note: Alternatives enter the matrix only after verified availability; missing alternatives are reported unavailable, never invented

published_notes: independently confirmed: the official Xiaomi release stores its experts natively as MXFP4; tacodevs card claim (not officially confirmed): experts are natively MXFP4 QAT and no BF16 expert release exists
baseline_precision_reference.interpretation_rule: Published allocation is evidence for sensitivity prioritization only: tensors allocated higher bits (8-bit non-expert text tensors; native MXFP4 and 3-bit vs 2-bit expert projections) are the published plan's implicit sensitivity ordering. It is NOT measured sensitivity, NOT our allocation, and NOT task-success evidence.

claims_and_prohibitions: No inference functionality is claimed anywhere in this design; nothing runs until weights, runtime and hardware prerequisites exist.
Fit claims use exact bytes only; no prose-unit memory matching.
Missing measurements stay null/unavailable; they are never zero and never inferred.
Published metrics stay labeled as distribution evidence, never task success.
Golden heldout long task success is the only decisive quality metric.

Feasibility math gate honored: at >= 4.25 bpw a 160-expert arm cannot fit A's exact cap (see feasibility_math_gate); unequal weight budgets are never silently called memory matched, and A remains the mandatory static control.
